plan.title: Zebrafish larvae drug exposure DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: Salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples: 3 drug-treated vs 3 control zebrafish larvae pools, unpaired, single batch) are analyzed with the standard DESeq2 workflow for a 2-group, n=3/group design: sample-structure QC first to check that treated and control separate and no sample is an outlier, then a minimal low-count pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization internal to DESeq2, an explicit-reference-level model (control as reference) with a Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2 fold change, and BH-FDR selection at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering. Because n=3/group gives limited power, the report step states the expected power explicitly and does not loosen thresholds to compensate. Danio rerio has no curated MSigDB collection in this environment, so pathway interpretation proceeds by mapping zebrafish gene symbols to their one-to-one human orthologs (org.Dr.eg.db / babelgene) and running preranked fgsea (ranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic) against the human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets staged in this environment, reporting the ortholog mapping rate and the enrichment method's caveats explicitly. A final report step consolidates DE results, diagnostics, and pathway hits with full reproducibility metadata.

zebrafish human ortholog mapping gene set enrichment analysis babelgene

~condition, explicit reference level = control, contrast treated_vs_control
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha=0.05
Map zebrafish gene symbols to human orthologs (org.Dr.eg.db/babelgene), then fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald stat against MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets
Integrated DE + enrichment report with power caveat for n=3/group
